Subject: POC success criteria & KPIs - Atlas Payments

Thanks Priya — great conversation today. Per our call, here’s a proposed set of success criteria, evaluation plan, and next steps for the POC/trial. Please review and confirm or call out any items we should adjust.

Proposed success criteria / KPIs:
- Latency: p95 <= 300ms for typical requests (~512 tokens) under target load
- Throughput: sustain 10 req/s per instance with burst capacity to 25 req/s
- Cost: target cost/token <= $0.0005 (tokenization model TBD)
- Quality: >= 90% semantic match on a 500-query evaluation set provided by Atlas (measured by manual labels + automated metrics)
- Reliability: error rate < 0.5% and end-to-end availability >= 99.9% during test window

Evaluation plan (high level):
1) Integration & baseline (Week 0-1): connect test harness, send initial dataset, run baseline with current config
2) Load & latency testing (Week 1-2): run sustained throughput tests to validate p95 and throughput SLOs
3) Quality evaluation (Week 2-3): run the 500-query eval set, collect manual labels for a 100-sample subset to validate semantic match
4) Tuning & handoff (Week 3-4): apply batching/quantization/config tuning and re-run key tests for sign-off

Ownership:
- Atlas: provide evaluation dataset, test endpoints, procurement lead (Priya)
- Redwood Sales: Jordan Blake — commercial coordination & signoff
- Redwood Solutions/CS: Marissa Cole — technical lead, test harness and tuning
- Redwood Security: Neha Kapoor — SOC2 / compliance artifacts & security intake

Next steps:
- Tech deep-dive / integration call: propose Tue Aug 3 or Wed Aug 4 (please confirm)
- I’ll share a draft POC plan and security questionnaire (attached)
- Atlas to confirm procurement timeline and any additional acceptance criteria (PCI scope, data retention rules)

Attachments: redwood-poc-plan-v1.pdf (draft POC plan)

Thanks — Jordan
Jordan Blake

On Sat, Jul 31, 2027 at 10:12 AM Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
> Proposed success criteria / KPIs:
> - Latency: p95 <= 300ms ...

Thanks — looping in the technical plan below and next steps from Redwood’s side. I’ve attached the draft POC plan and the security questionnaire stub for Atlas to complete.

Redwood POC plan (detailed):
Week 0 (integration & baseline)
- Task: Exchange API keys / test creds, integrate SDK, sanity checks on request/response
- Deliverable: Baseline latency/throughput snapshot, integration checklist

Week 1 (load & latency)
- Task: Run sustained load at target throughput (10 req/s) and measure p50/p95/p99; identify hotspots
- Deliverable: Load test report + recommended config (batching, KV cache settings)

Week 2 (quality evaluation)
- Task: Run 500-query eval; sample 100 responses for manual labeling; compute semantic match and precision/recall where applicable
- Deliverable: Quality report with failure-mode examples and suggested prompt tweaks

Week 3 (tuning & sign-off)
- Task: Apply tuning (quantization/profile changes, batching adjustments), re-run critical tests, and finalize acceptance metrics
- Deliverable: Final report & sign-off checklist

Acceptance criteria mapping (examples):
- Latency: p95 <= 300ms after tuning AND under defined load
- Throughput: 10 req/s sustained with <1% error rate
- Quality: >= 90% semantic match on the evaluation set; manual review sample must have <=10% false positives

Attachments: redwood-poc-plan-v1.pdf, atlas-security-questionnaire.xlsx

Next steps (action items)
- Jordan: send calendar invite for Aug 3 10:00am PT (tech deep-dive)
- Priya: confirm dataset delivery timeline and legal NDA addendum
- Neha: prepare SOC2 artifacts and PCI scoping notes

I’ll start the test harness repo and share the initial scripts before the call.
